title: Streaming anomaly detection & alerting for usage / cost / latency metrics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: implement robust streaming anomaly detection and alerting for key console metrics (per-customer usage, per-route cost, and p50/p95 latency) in the backend analytics pipeline so that SRE/Platform/Customer Success get timely, accurate signals about regressions or billing anomalies. Scope covers backend pipeline changes, alerting rules, routing to PagerDuty/Slack/Console-notifications, and a minimal tuning UI in the Console for on-call engineers and account owners.

Background: We currently surface aggregated daily usage/cost dashboards from the analytics pipeline but lack near-real-time anomaly detection. That causes slow incident detection for sudden regressions (e.g., sudden token cost runaways, regression-caused latency spikes, or misconfigured clients generating traffic). This ticket designs and implements a streaming-first detection system integrated into our Kafka -> Airflow -> Snowflake pipeline and real-time alert router.

Core requirements: detect both spike and drift anomalies, support multi-tenant per-customer baselines, ignore known maintenance windows and billing cycle-induced fluctuations, keep false positive rate low (<5% by default), and produce alerts within 5 minutes of detection for streaming metrics. Alerts must include context (delta, baseline, recent examples, example requests if available) and link to runbooks/dashboard panels.

Approach summary: implement an ensemble of lightweight detectors in the analytics-service (golang) for streaming events and a batch reanalysis job for aggregation anomalies: 1) streaming EWMA + robust z-score for immediate spikes, 2) rolling median absolute deviation (MAD) with dynamic windowing for outliers, 3) seasonal decomposition fallback (daily/weekly) run in the nightly Airflow job to update seasonal baselines. The streaming detectors will emit anomaly events to an alerting Kafka topic which the alert-router consumes and maps to PagerDuty/Slack/Console notifications using tenant routing rules. Thresholds are tenant-aware and default to baseline+k*MAD but can be overridden per-customer via Console.

Non-goals: full ML-based anomaly classification in this sprint, long-term model training infra, UI-heavy threshold management (we'll add a minimal slider and a link to advanced settings).

Notes on data and privacy: only emit aggregated summaries for multi-tenant anomalies; for high-severity alerts that require request samples, we will redact PII and include a secure link to a short-lived diagnostic artifact stored in the secure diagnostics bucket.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming detector deployed to analytics-service producing anomaly events to topic alerts.anomalies
Alert-router consumes alerts.anomalies and fires PagerDuty alerts and Slack spike messages with runbook links
Per-tenant default thresholds applied and visible in Console settings (minimal UI)
False positive rate on historical replay < 5% (measured on last 90 days of telemetry for top 50 tenants)
Alert end-to-end latency < 5 minutes from event ingestion to notification in PagerDuty
Include a Confluence runbook with triage steps and sample dashboards linked from alerts
implementation_notes: Streaming detectors implemented in golang module analytics-service/pkg/anomaly
Use Kafka topic 'metrics.events' as canonical stream; enricher service must attach tenant_id and route tags (ENG-4671)
Lightweight detectors run on each partition; state stored in RocksDB-based local store with TTL for baseline windows
Nightly Airflow job 'analytics.seasonal_baseline' writes seasonal baselines to Snowflake table analytics.seasonal_baselines
Alert-router will deduplicate anomalies within 10m window to avoid alert storms
Provide feature flag (ff_anomaly_v1) to gate rollout per-tenant / per-environment
Add metric 'anomaly.alerts.fired' to observability and create a Console dashboard for alert volume and precision over time
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: alert storms during initial rollout -> mitigation: aggressive dedupe + progressive rollout via feature flag
Risk: seasonal/business events causing false positives (billing or invoice runs) -> mitigation: integration with deployment calendar and billing windows to mute detections
Risk: compute cost on streaming nodes increases -> mitigation: cap per-tenant memory for baseline state and sample heavy tenants into a heavier path
Risk: sensitive data exposure in alert context -> mitigation: only send aggregated context by default and redact PII in any request samples. Secure links require strong auth and short TTLs
testing_plan: Unit tests for detectors (z-score, EWMA, MAD) with synthetic datasets
Integration test: replay 90 days of metrics into test Kafka cluster and assert alert counts and precision
Chaos test: simulate Kafka partition shift and ensure state recovery (RocksDB TTL behaviour)
End-to-end staging test: verify PagerDuty and Slack payloads and dedupe behavior
A/B rollout to 10 pilot tenants and collect feedback from CS/SRE for 2 weeks before broader rollout
migration_and_rollout: Start with internal tenants and Platform team (feature flag on) for 1 week
Gradual 25/50/100% rollout over subsequent 2 weeks depending on false positive metrics
After rollout, schedule follow-up ticket for UI improvements and advanced rules (ENG-4792)
